phrases.value: Hello, I am Jessica Mestre-Jeffrey, Student Success Manager with Empowered for College.
This video is the second in a two-part series all about values.
If you joined Empowered for College as a sophomore, you will need to complete the freshman module and reflection first in order to understand the sophomore module.
We'll begin with a brief synopsis for those of you who watched part one in this series a year ago.
Values are the principles and beliefs by which we live our lives.

Values matter because they provide us with purpose, individuality, a sense of direction, a guide for decision-making, a way to determine how we use our resources, and a life in alignment with what we find important.

If you watched the original video last year, hopefully you have posted your top values somewhere visible and have found opportunities to incorporate your values into daily life since completing the original module.
This video will help you further explore how you want to incorporate these values into your future life.
First, let's think about how values can show up in college.
Today's worksheet includes these reflection prompts.
How do my values relate to the type of university or college I want to attend?
How could my values influence what major and classes I choose?
How might my values affect my college involvement?
Please pause the video, take as much time as you need to complete that section of the worksheet, and then restart the video.
Now that you have reflected on values in college, let's think about values in your career.
How could your values show up in a future career?
If you have a sense of your career aspirations already, think of each value in that specific work environment.
If you're exploring career interests, see if you can think of examples of careers that would align well with a particular value.
For example, if you chose helping others as a top five value, you could focus your career goals around that.
Or, you could choose to spend your personal time volunteering and take a different direction with your career.
As another example, if I chose flexibility as one of my values, the list of relevant careers might include freelance work or being an entrepreneur.
However, if I chose stability as a top value, instead that would translate well to being an accountant or working in healthcare.
To be clear, this is just a creative brainstorming exercise.
Please pause the video here and take whatever time you need to reflect on each of your top five values connected to your career.
Thank you for taking the time to reflect on values in college and career settings.
Sometimes reflections like this can feel a bit intimidating or overwhelming.
In case you're feeling that way, I want to encourage you to be patient.
Students frequently change their major in college.
Many graduates pursue work unrelated to their major, and it is possible to pivot mid-career if your original choice ends up not being a great fit.
It's easy to get bogged down in the what and how of a career, but taking time to understand the why of it all will increase your chances of finding fulfillment.
Again, I hope this reflection on values was an insightful experience for you all.
If you have any questions or concerns, please email me.
Take good care!
